Planning only. No code changes made.

One concrete note before the plan: your prompt says “post-review-session-redesign branch,” but this checkout currently reports `main`. I treated this as continuing the post-redesign UI planning work from the current tree plus the April 15, 2026 handoff docs.

**Reusable Contracts**
- The launch/preflight contract is already good enough to keep unchanged. [`resolveStudioNewReviewPreflight`](</Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts:217>) and the proxied `/api/studio/new-review/preflight` route already expose `startability`, `contextMode`, `commitSha`, `checks`, warnings, and blocking issues. See [studio-create.ts](</Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts:34>) and [ui-proxy.ts](</Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/ui-proxy.ts:764>).
- The launch action contract is reusable unchanged. [`startStudioNewReview`](</Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts:435>) already emits staged progress, preserves branch-context safety, returns `sessionId`, and hands back a canonical `routePath` for routing. The SSE proxy for that is already in [ui-proxy.ts](</Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/ui-proxy.ts:841>).
- The session object is the right primary UI object and already has the fields we need: phase, pass count, current status, outcome, and pass summaries. See [types.ts](</Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/types.ts:247>) and [types.ts](</Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/types.ts:577>).
- The live session aggregate contract is already strong enough for slices 2 and 3. [`loadStudioSessionAggregate`](</Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/ui-proxy.ts:369>) already composes session, reviews, findings rollup, activity snapshot, reviewed diff availability, local environments, and capabilities into one UI-facing payload.
- The activity model is reusable unchanged. The session activity snapshot and streamed entries already distinguish active vs waiting vs terminal and normalize live events into `policy | progress | finding | remediation | terminal | status`. See [ui-proxy.ts](</Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/ui-proxy.ts:491>) and [types.ts](</Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/types.ts:495>).
- The reviewed diff contract is reusable unchanged. [`/api/studio/sessions/:id/reviewed-diff`](</Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/ui-proxy.ts:945>) already tells us whether a remediated diff exists and returns proper `WorkspaceDiffResponse` data when it does.
- The adopt contract is reusable unchanged, including the product semantics. Adoption stays user-facing as `adopt`, creates an isolated worktree or branch, and refuses active/non-ready sessions. See [materialize.ts](</Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/materialize.ts:240>) and [ui-proxy.ts](</Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/ui-proxy.ts:1081>).
- Merge-back is also already the right contract for slice 4. The proxy exposes `/merge-back`, and the CLI behavior already matches the intended human-in-the-loop model. See [ui-proxy.ts](</Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/ui-proxy.ts:1158>).

**Very Small Rebuild Plan**
- Rebuild only the `/` route first as a new current-state launch experience.
- Treat the existing home/report/history UI as disposable. Do not preserve its component structure just because it exists.
- Keep only two first-class destinations in the new IA for now: `/` and `/sessions/:sessionId`.
- Let all other existing routes survive only as compatibility redirects or deferred cleanup, not as product-shaping surfaces.
- Do not add new backend work for slice 1 unless we hit a real implementation snag.

**Experience 1: Current-State Launch**
- `Page purpose:` Answer one honest question: “What should happen for the current `HEAD` right now?” Either launch a session, explain why launch is blocked, or immediately route into the already-existing session for that commit.
- `Required data:` `GET /api/studio/context`, `GET /api/studio/new-review/preflight?lastCheckpoints=1`, and `GET /api/review-sessions?repo=<repo>&branch=<branch>` with client-side selection by `anchorCommitSha === preflight.commitSha`. No new contract required.
- `Core state 1:` booting. The page shows a compact resolver state, not a fake dashboard.
- `Core state 2:` not in a git repo / repo context unavailable. Show a single blocked card with no start CTA.
- `Core state 3:` existing session found for current commit. Do not show “new review.” Show a brief “Opening current session” interstitial, then `replace`-navigate into that session.
- `Core state 4:` ready in `intent_aware` mode. Show a minimal launch card with one primary CTA: `Start review session`.
- `Core state 5:` ready in `basic` mode. Same launch card, but clearly downgraded copy, explicit fallback language, and a learn-more link for Entire.
- `Core state 6:` blocked. Show the blocking reason plainly and no optimistic affordances.
- `Core state 7:` launch in progress. Replace the launch CTA with a bounded stage list driven by the start SSE stream.
- `Transition rules:` On load, resolve current context and preflight. If a matching session exists, route immediately. If not, render the launch state. On focus or visibility return, silently re-check. While launch is in progress, lock the page to the launch stream. On completed launch event, navigate to returned `routePath`. If branch/repo drift is detected, fall back to a hard visible “context changed” state and force a fresh preflight.
- `Routing behavior:` `/` is not a dashboard anymore. It is a resolver. Its only job is to forward the user to the current session or offer a truthful start surface for current `HEAD`.
- `Copy tone:` Calm, operational, and literal. No “magic” framing. Good examples: “Nimbus will review the current commit.” “Entire context is unavailable. Nimbus can still start in basic mode.” “This commit already has an active review session.”
- `Layout structure:` Single-column page, roughly 760-840px max width. Top strip: repo, branch, commit. Main card: launch or blocked state. Secondary card: preflight facts. During launch, the main card becomes a compact stage feed. No side nav. No history table. No secondary marketing copy.
- `Visual direction:` Use the skill’s “Minimal Single Column” and developer-tool typography, but not the skill’s loud vibrant style. I’d use JetBrains Mono sparingly for labels, commit/session identifiers, and stage rows, with IBM Plex Sans for body/UI copy. The overall feel should be light and spare, with one darker inset surface for launch progress so the later live session page feels continuous.
- `Color direction:` Neutral light shell, slate/ink text, clear border rhythm, green only for successful readiness, amber for `basic`, red for blocked/error. Avoid neon, glow, or full-app dark-mode theatrics.
- `Restrained motion plan:` 180-220ms page fade/settle on first load, 120-160ms card/state swaps, staged row reveals only when real start events arrive, and no ambient looping motion. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- `What to omit on purpose:` No review history list. No branch browsing. No report links. No pass history. No policy mode toggle. No checkpoint window selector. No artifact browsing. No findings preview. No secondary “new review” paths once a session exists for `HEAD`.

**Next 3 Experiences**
- `2. Live session page:` One primary surface with phase/status at top, a bounded terminal-style live log, and findings appearing as they materialize. Do not render terminal outcome chrome while the session is still active. This can sit directly on top of [`StudioSessionAggregateResponse`](</Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/types.ts:577>) plus `/activity/events`.
- `3. Reviewed diff experience:` This is a terminal-session view, not a separate report product. If `reviewedDiff.available`, show a real diff viewer. If not, say plainly: Nimbus did not produce a remediated result, so there is nothing to adopt. No artifact archaeology.
- `4. Adopt / merge-back experience:` Make `Adopt locally` the first explicit handoff. Explain that Nimbus creates an isolated local worktree and switches the user into that testable result. After adoption, show local diff, local environment status, and `Merge back into current branch`. Keep PR creation out entirely.

**Real Gap**
- The only real contract wrinkle I found is that “is there already a session for current `HEAD`?” is currently assembled client-side by combining repo/branch session listing with `anchorCommitSha` filtering. That is acceptable for slice 1 and not a blocker. If we later want to harden or simplify, we can add a dedicated current-state endpoint, but I would not delay the rebuild for it.
